name: Standing-order / mandate row
purpose: A RECURRING PAYMENT INSTRUCTION THAT HAS NOT HAPPENED YET: who is paid, how much, on what rhythm, when next, and what state the instruction is in. Two actions per row — open the mandate, or manage it. PROPOSED #209 (itinerary row 95, slug standing-order-mandate-row, P3) — NOT GATED, NOT RULED. Fintech semantics are Dave's (the Kpi-tile precedent, s182-D2).

props.name: payee
props.$note: The row's subject. It must never be the element that gives way when chips crowd the line — see antiPatterns and knownFindings.

props.name: mandateType
props.$note: ⛔ NOT COSMETIC. A standing order is the customer's own instruction (fixed amount, fixed rhythm, the customer controls it); a Direct Debit is a mandate granted to a PAYEE who pulls a VARIABLE amount under the Direct Debit Guarantee. Legally and operationally different objects. Rendered as a Tags atom (square outline chip) IN TEXT — never by hue, never by an icon alone. Whether they should be ONE component or TWO is DAVE'S (P3); drawing them in one list does not settle it.

props.name: amount
props.$note: MONOCHROME, always. Amount-display's format via Runway-bar: symbol before the amount with no space (copy-025), tabular lining figures, U+2212 for the minus. No coloured monetary seat is bound anywhere in this component.

props.name: amountIsVariable
props.$note: PROPOSED, NOT RULED (P2). A variable Direct Debit shows the LAST taken figure and says 'Amount varies' in the rhythm line, rather than presenting a stale number as if it were the next one. Which figure a variable mandate should show is Dave's.

props.name: rhythm
props.$note: PROPOSED, NOT RULED (P2). 'Monthly on the 1st' / 'Weekly on Fridays' / 'Monthly, around the 14th'. Alternatives: a bare next date, a countdown ('in 11 days'), or a rhythm carrying its end ('until 20 August 2026', drawn on one specimen).

props.name: nextDate
props.$note: The row's date is in the FUTURE and is a PROMISE — that is the tell against the gated transaction row, whose date is in the past and is a fact.

props.name: status
props.$note: PROPOSED, NOT RULED (P4). Rendered as a Status-indicator RAG-tint chip ALWAYS CARRYING ITS WORD; 'active' draws NO chip, because a list of twelve green chips is noise. ⛔ 'failed' sits on the WARNING seat, not the error seat — deliberate restraint, NOT a considered ruling: the error seat touches the two-red law (s151-D1) and is Dave's.

props.name: consequence
props.$note: A plain text line under the body on the failed row ('Not enough money on 12 June. We will try again on 19 June.'), role="status". The consequence is TEXT, never a hue.

props.name: manageAction
props.$note: PROPOSED, NOT RULED (P5). Drawn as a trailing 44×44 icon-button carrying the byte-matched global-controls/menu-more-horizontal.svg glyph with an accessible name. Alternatives Dave may prefer: a text button ('Manage'), no control at all with the actions on the detail page, or a real Dropdown menu.

variants.name: standing-order
variants.use: Fixed amount, fixed rhythm, the customer's own instruction. Shows sort code and account ending.

variants.name: direct-debit
variants.use: The payee pulls. Shows the service-user reference, and 'Amount varies' where the next figure is unknown.

variants.name: paused
variants.use: Still yours, still returns. The row is NOT dimmed — a paused mandate is live information.

variants.name: failed
variants.use: The last payment did not go through. A WORD on the warning seat plus a plain consequence line. No red.

variants.name: ending-soon
variants.use: A mandate with an end condition: '2 payments left', 'until 20 August 2026'.

variants.name: cancelled
variants.use: History. FULLY LEGIBLE, with a 'Cancelled' chip; only the control is disabled. See the $renderFinding — the dimmed version was drawn and could not be read.

tokens.surface: tertiary/background/default — the list shell and rows
tokens.hover: tertiary/background/hover — row hover; the leading glyph flips to the surface so it separates from the tint (List-items' trick)
tokens.muted: text/secondary — the rhythm line, the 'next' line, the type tag
tokens.icon: icon/default — the leading glyph and the manage control
tokens.status: rag/warning + rag/warning-tint (paused, failed) | rag/information + rag/information-tint (ending soon, cancelled) | rag/success + rag/success-tint (declared, unused — 'active' draws no chip)
tokens.focus: focus/ring — 2px outline, offset -2, on the stretched link and the manage button
tokens.opacity: alpha/72 on secondary text and the resting control; alpha/48 on the cancelled row's glyph; alpha/40 on the disabled control
tokens.radius: border-radius/surface (the list shell) + border-radius/indicator (tag, chip, control). 0 in Mono and Legacy; Console forks surface through the cascade.
tokens.$note: NO NEW TOKEN IS WANTED OR MINTED. Every value here already exists and is already bound by a gated component. ⛔ NO COLOURED MONETARY SEAT IS BOUND: every amount is text/default.

$renderFinding: ⚠⚠ TWO DEFECTS WERE FOUND BY LOOKING AT THE RENDER AT #209, AND EVERY GATE WAS GREEN OVER BOTH. (1) THE CANCELLED ROW: the draft copied Document-row's DISABLED treatment — text/disabled on every text element, which in LIGHT is #E1E1E1 on #FFFFFF, 1.42:1 — and the whole row, payee included, was an unreadable ghost. No gate fires because disabled content is exempt from 1.4.3 (the same class Document-row caught at #204 on its GLYPH; here it had swallowed the TEXT). THE FIX IS A CATEGORY CORRECTION, NOT A COLOUR TWEAK: a cancelled mandate is not disabled content, it is HISTORY — you must still be able to read who you were paying and when you stopped. The row is now ordinary ink with a 'Cancelled' chip, and only the CONTROL is disabled. Whether it should be dimmed at all is P9, Dave's. (2) THE CRUSHED PAYEE: with the title line as a non-wrapping flex row, the tag and status chips were flex:none and the payee was the only shrinkable item, so rows carrying both chips crushed the name to 'Bristol …' and 'Kestrel Ass…'. Measured before/after in a real browser at 560px: payee element widths 66–175px BEFORE, 204–227px AFTER. The line now wraps and the payee claims a 160px basis.

motion.hover: Row background to tertiary/background/hover, and the control's opacity to alpha/96, over the inherited 140ms ease.

responsive.rule: Container-query reflow at 360c: the row wraps, the payee takes a full line and the money block drops beneath it (WCAG 1.4.10) — List-items' and Document-row's own behaviour. Verified in a real browser at 1400px and at a 340px container.

livesInside: Standing orders and Direct Debits list

accessibility.role: A <ul> of PASSIVE <li> rows, each holding a stretched-link primary (<a> whose ::after covers the row) and a SIBLING <button>. Document-row's shape, copied: nesting an interactive control inside a <button> is invalid (4.1.1), unreachable in several ATs, and swallows the inner accessible name.
accessibility.name: The list carries aria-label. Each manage button carries a full accessible name naming the payee and the state ('Manage the standing order to Bristol Trade Supplies, last payment failed').
accessibility.twoTargets: DRIVEN IN A REAL BROWSER at #209, not asserted: document.elementFromPoint at each row's centre returns the stretched <a>; at each button's centre it returns the button's own content; every button box measures 44×44; Tab order alternates link → button per row (14 focusables across 8 drawn rows, the cancelled row's button being natively disabled).
accessibility.failureNote: role="status" (polite), not role="alert": the failure already happened and the row is being read, not interrupted.
accessibility.notColourAlone: Every state carries its WORD in the chip and its consequence in text. The mandate TYPE is a word, never a hue. Remove all colour and the component still says everything it means (1.4.1).
accessibility.hitArea: ≥44px on every interactive target, ENFORCED BY HAND AND MEASURED — no gate reads the ruled 44px token from a snippet. Primary target = the stretched-link row (min-height 76, measured 79 with padding). Manage button = 44×44 measured.

antiPatterns: ⛔ FLATTENING STANDING ORDER AND DIRECT DEBIT INTO ONE UNDIFFERENTIATED 'RECURRING PAYMENT'. They are different objects with different control and different legal protection. The row says which one IN TEXT.
⛔ NESTING THE MANAGE CONTROL INSIDE A WHOLE-ROW BUTTON. Invalid HTML (4.1.1); the inner control becomes unreachable and its accessible name is absorbed. Use the stretched-link + sibling-button shape.
⛔ PAINTING A FAILED PAYMENT RED. The error seat touches the two-red law (s151-D1) and is Dave's. The word and the consequence line carry it here.
⛔ DIMMING A CANCELLED MANDATE INTO ILLEGIBILITY. It is history you may still need to read. See $renderFinding.
Showing a stale figure as if it were the next payment on a variable Direct Debit. Say 'Amount varies'.
Letting a status chip crush the payee name. The payee is the subject; the line wraps instead.
Relying on the status DOT to convey state. The dot is 1.98:1 / 2.18:1 standalone (measured #204); the word is the carrier.
Colouring the amount. No monetary colour seat is bound in this component.

$differsFrom.List-items (type=transaction): GATED, PROMOTED, 9.0/9. A transaction is a payment that HAS HAPPENED: one date, one amount, a settled balance effect. A mandate is an instruction that HAS NOT HAPPENED: a rhythm, a future date, an end condition, and a state you can change. THE TELL: you cannot pause a transaction. A mandate row carrying only a payee and an amount IS a List-items row and should be one.
$differsFrom.Document-row: Same ROW SHAPE, copied wholesale (passive li + stretched link + sibling button + list shell + the disabled-glyph lesson). Different subject: a document is an object you can only read; a mandate is an instruction you can alter.
$differsFrom.Transaction-row (the ledger, same lane #: That component states what the balance became. This one states what is going to happen and when. Neither carries the other's discriminator.
$differsFrom.Timeline / Countdown-timer: Those render time itself. This renders a payment whose next occurrence happens to be a date.

$decisionsForDave: The mandate-type vocabulary: 'Standing order' / 'Direct Debit' — the real UK terms — or 'Recurring payment' / 'Subscription'?
One component or two for standing order vs Direct Debit?
Does 'Last payment failed' belong on the ERROR seat rather than the warning seat? Deliberately not taken — it touches the two-red law.
For a variable Direct Debit: show the last taken figure (as drawn), the next estimate, or no figure?
Does an ACTIVE mandate carry a chip at all? Drawn silent.
The trailing control: icon-only (as drawn), a text 'Manage' button, a Dropdown menu, or nothing?
Does the payee's account detail belong on the row or only on the detail page?
Should a CANCELLED row be dimmed? It is not dimmed here because the dimmed version was drawn, rendered, and could not be read.
The leading glyph: no recurring-payment glyph exists in the library (probe in knownFindings). Is an icon-gap entry owed, or should the slot hold a payee avatar instead?
